ActExpr.description:
An action inside an expression: the action forms that may nest, with
expression arguments.

ActKind.description:
What an [`Expr::Act`] does. `yield` and `cancel` stay statement
actions.

oneOf.description: Calls a function and yields what it returns.
Runs one effect and yields its result, decoded as `result`.
Waits for a number of milliseconds, its one argument.
Starts a task running a function and yields its handle.
Waits on the task handle that is its one argument.
Waits on the list of task handles that is its one argument.
Gives other ready tasks their turn.
Cancels the task handle that is its one argument.
Awaits its one argument by the await policy (`K-TASK-026`).

Action.description:
An action as the whole right-hand side of its own statement, its
arguments atoms (`K-FORM-001`); [`Expr::Act`] nests one in an
expression.

oneOf.description: Calls a function and yields what it returns.
Runs one effect and yields its result, decoded as `result`.

then_yield.description:
Whether the task takes one more turn of the ready queue once
the outcome is in, before it continues (`K-TASK-005`).

oneOf.description: Waits for a number of milliseconds.
Waits on one task handle.
Waits on a list of task handles.
Lets every other ready task run first.
Starts a task running a function and yields its handle.
Raises a cancellation in a task at its current wait.

Awaits a value by its dialect's await policy: a library function
that takes the value, waits as the dialect's `await` does, and
yields what the `await` gives (`K-TASK-026`).

AssignOrder.description:
The order an assignment to a member evaluates its parts in
(`K-EVAL-003`): each dialect's own, written in the document.

oneOf.description:
The right-hand side, then the place's target, then its index, as
Python assigns.

The place's target, then its index, then the right-hand side, as
TypeScript assigns. Only a member is written in this order, and its
right-hand side is an expression: an action there is nested.

Atom.description: An argument of an action: a variable or a literal, never a computation.

Callee.description: What a call or a `spawn` runs.

oneOf.description: A declared function of the document, by name.
The closure or function reference a variable holds.
A library function, by identity.

binding.description: The variable the caught error value is bound to.

Closure.description:
A function value written in place. It shares the variables of the scope
that defines it (`K-CLO-001`); which ones is derived, never written.

start.description:
How a value this closure makes is started when it crosses to a tool
as a [`crate::FunctionValue`] (`K-CLO-004`); `None` for one that
cannot be started. Executable behaviour: it is part of the
document's identity.

DataValue.description: Data that can be connected to a value slot; no executable syntax.

Expr.description:
An expression, evaluated within one statement. Only an [`Expr::Act`]
in it may pause the task (`K-EVAL-008`).

oneOf.description: Evaluates the condition, then only the selected branch.
Evaluates `value` before binding `name`, visible only in `body`.
Reads a field or an index.
Calls a library function that has a native implementation.
The embedder's clock, as a timestamp.
A float drawn by the embedder, uniform in `[0, 1)`.
Reads through a projection handle.

An action nested in the expression: the statement may pause at it,
the operands it has already evaluated kept as the roles of its
continuation (`K-EVAL-008`).

FunctionRepresentation.description: How a dialect holds a function as a value.

oneOf.description: The closure itself.

A tuple whose first member is the text `tag` and whose member at
`callable` is the closure. The tuple crosses as one function value.
Every member has ended, or the first failure.
Every member has ended.
The first member to end.
The first member to succeed.
A reference to a declared function of the document.

Member.description: A field of a record or an index into a collection.

Name.description:
A variable, parameter or declared-function name.

Any text is a name; the kernel gives none of them meaning. Structural
validation refuses the empty name.

optional.description:
The argument may be omitted, and is then absent (`K-FN-004`). No
required parameter follows an optional one.

Position.description:
Where a statement is put: in `block`, ahead of the statement `before`,
or at the block's end.

request.description: What is asked of the projection: kernel data the host interprets.

Protocol.description:
A dialect's iteration protocol: the library functions a `for … via`
calls at its header, by identity (`K-ITER-005`). Each is listed in the
manifest as any library function a document reaches.

check.description:
Checks a map or a set against its size when the loop opened it and
the items it may still give, after each step; gives that budget
anew.

item.description: Takes what was walked and an item of it to the value bound.

next.description:
Steps a driver: an empty tuple when it is exhausted, else a tuple of
one item.

open.description:
Takes the iterated value to what the loop walks: a list, a tuple, a
map, a set or a text, which the loop's own cursor walks, or any
other value, a driver that `next` steps.

rest.description:
The type of every field not named in `fields`. `None` closes the
record: it has no other field.

Rhs.description: The right-hand side of a `let` or an assignment.

Signature.description: What a function, an effect or an entry takes and returns.

Site.description:
A node's address: the code it belongs to and the chain of
[`Node::children`] indexes that reaches it from that code's body.

A site is derived from the document and is never written by a host
(`K-ID-004`). An empty chain addresses the body itself.

StartAdapter.description:
How a function a closure makes is started from outside its run: the
signature it is started under, how the dialect holds the function as a
value, and how the entry calls it.

StartConvention.description:
How a host starts an entry. A start adapter uses the same convention
when it extracts a function value from a dialect callable.

oneOf.description:
With the start's arguments, in the signature's order, returning what
the function returns.

Source parameters are bound directly; extra start arguments are
discarded, missing ones are absent, and an absent result becomes null.
When extracting a packed TypeScript callable, `await_fn` settles its
result before the entry returns.

With an absent `this` and the list of the start's arguments; the
returned value is awaited by `await_fn`, and an absent result
(`same_fn` compares it with absent) ends the start with null.

As `Direct`, and the run's root cleanup: when the entry's body has
left, by its return or its raise, and its own `finally` blocks have
run, `cleanup` is called with no arguments before the run ends. The
body's departure then ends the run, unless the cleanup raises: its
raise does instead. Python's `asyncio.run` cancels and waits for the
tasks still running this way (`K-TASK-019`).
Declares a variable in the enclosing block and gives it a value.

Writes a variable, a field or an index, evaluating its parts in
`order` (`K-EVAL-003`).

Removes a field of a record, an element of a list, an entry of a map
or a member of a set.
Evaluates an expression for effect and discards its result.

Runs `body` once per element of a collection, binding each to
`binding`, then `else_block` unless a `break` left the loop. With
`via`, a dialect's protocol opens the iterated value and steps it
(`K-ITER-005`).

Runs `body` while `condition` holds, then `else_block` unless a
`break` left the loop.

Evaluates the value, unwinds source cleanup, then calls `policy`
with the surviving value. The policy may wait; its result returns
directly, outside the source function's handlers.
Ends the run with a result.
Ends the run as failed, with a reason.
Every value.

An integer or a float. In an effect's result this is the bare number
the document's number policy decodes (`K-EFF-006`).
A tuple of exactly these member types.
A text that is one of these.
A closure or a function reference that takes and returns these.
A task handle whose task ends with this.
A handle of this host kind.
A value of any one of these types. Two or more, none itself a union.

Unit.description: The code a node belongs to.

oneOf.description: The document's `main`.
A declared function of the document.
The kernel-code body of a library function.

ValueTarget.description: All addresses are exact sites in the operation's base document.

path.description: Canonical child indices within the argument, empty for its root.

oneOf.description: A new try has an empty catch and no finally.

description:
Every supported canvas operation, admitted atomically through [`crate::Draft::apply`].
Structural operations accept only separable perform/tool steps. While loops
support condition editing; creating or removing one requires source.
